painting-mss.name: drawing
painting-mss.title: drawing
painting-mss.reason: This is a watercolor self-portrait drawing by Hilis Hadjo (Josiah Francis), a Creek (Muscogee) leader, depicting himself in regalia with pipe, pistol, belt and coat — a traditional-era work made by a member of the claimed culture.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a Creek (Muscogee) man in period shirt and trousers, documentary photo of dress consistent with the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of "Little Tiger," a named Native American man photographed in Washington DC, identified in the record as Muscogee; he wears a mix of Euro-American clothing and a blanket, consistent with documentary photographs of delegation visits by Native individuals to the capital in the 19th century.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of the Stidham family, prominent Muscogee (Creek) citizens, shown in Victorian-era dress documenting their daily life/social standing in this period; documentary photos of a people's dress or life count as belonging even in Western clothing.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Creek (Muscogee) man in period dress, documenting an individual's appearance and clothing; a legitimate documentary photo of the claimed people.

garment.name: moccasin
garment.title: moccasin
garment.reason: A pair of skin moccasins with red silk thread decoration, attributed by the museum to a Creek (Muscogee) chief's complete dress. This matches the claimed ethnicity and category well.

garment.name: jacket
garment.title: jacket
garment.reason: A fringed hide jacket documented as part of a complete Muscogee (Creek) chief's dress, made by the Creek—consistent with historic Southeastern Woodlands hide garments.

garment.name: bag
garment.title: bag
garment.reason: A finger-woven beaded shoulder bag with strap, part of a documented Muscogee (Creek) chief's dress ensemble — a classic Southeastern woven sash-and-bag garment accessory.

garment.name: garter
garment.title: garter
garment.reason: A pair of beaded worsted-wool garters, part of a documented complete Muscogee (Creek) chief's dress ensemble, explicitly attributed to the Creek by the museum.

garment.name: belt
garment.title: belt
garment.reason: A woven worsted wool belt with braided/tasseled cords, part of a documented Muscogee (Creek) chief's dress ensemble held by the museum, attributed directly to the Creek. This is a garment/accessory made and worn by the claimed people.

instruments.name: Drum
instruments.title: Drum
instruments.reason: A red hide-covered wooden drum decorated with zigzag beadwork/quillwork patterns, labeled Creek (Muskogee family), a Southeastern Woodlands drum consistent with Muscogee ceremonial instruments.
